Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx FINANCIAL AID Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units. EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration TEST CREDIT If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit TRANSFER HELP Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors! Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4 Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar , on the first floor of University Hall ( interactive map link ).
notes.contentHtml:
This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: CONCENTRATIONS The Kinesiology major has 4 concentrations: Allied Health Professions (AHP), Exercise Science (ES), Health Promotion (HP), and Physical Education and Adapted Physical Education (PEAPE). MAJOR INFORMATION The concentration in Allied Health Professions (AHP) is for people interested in eventual graduate education in allied health professions (e.g., physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician’s assistant, medical or dental school) after graduation from CSUSB. CSUSB Kinesiology AHP students will engage in a rigorous course of study in Kinesiology, Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. This concentration offers undergraduate students essential pre-requisite courses for eventual graduate study in a preferred AHP. Students are strongly encouraged to review admission requirements at accredited universities to which they may apply for specific allied health professional graduate programs. Twelve units in the AHP concentration meets the requirements for GE and major. The department offers: • A variety of upper-division classes taught by faculty who are experts in their respective fields. • Hands on lab experiences that teach practical skills needed to be successful. • Life-long connections with enthusiastic faculty and students. • Extracurricular and co-curricular opportunities to enhance students’ educational experience. • Internal and external internships and field experiences to prepare students for their career. More information about our program, student accomplishments, faculty research activities, and advising information can be found on our website: https://www.csusb.edu/kinesiology ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/kinesiology/kinesiology-bs/ ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES **ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible. **SECTION 6 BELOW: This section displays three options for completing additional science requirements for this major. Group C is intended for students interested in pursuing a graduate degree to become a Physician Assistant. In addition to the lower-division courses listed, it requires one upper-division course. CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS Find out more about this major here: What is the Kinesiology Major? ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) This major does not have a corresponding Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT).

CONCENTRATIONS

The Kinesiology major has 4 concentrations: Allied Health Professions (AHP), Exercise Science (ES), Health Promotion (HP), and Physical Education and Adapted Physical Education (PEAPE).


MAJOR INFORMATION

The concentration in Allied Health Professions (AHP) is for people interested in eventual graduate education in allied health professions (e.g., physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician’s assistant, medical or dental school) after graduation from CSUSB. CSUSB Kinesiology AHP students will engage in a rigorous course of study in Kinesiology, Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. This concentration offers undergraduate students essential pre-requisite courses for eventual graduate study in a preferred AHP. Students are strongly encouraged to review admission requirements at accredited universities to which they may apply for specific allied health professional graduate programs. Twelve units in the AHP concentration meets the requirements for GE and major. 


The department offers:

• A variety of upper-division classes taught by faculty who are experts in their respective fields. 

• Hands on lab experiences that teach practical skills needed to be successful.

• Life-long connections with enthusiastic faculty and students.

• Extracurricular and co-curricular opportunities to enhance students’ educational experience.

• Internal and external internships and field experiences to prepare students for their career. 


More information about our program, student accomplishments, faculty research activities, and advising information can be found on our website: https://www.csusb.edu/kinesiology


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/kinesiology/kinesiology-bs/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

  • **ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information.  It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.
  • **SECTION 6 BELOW: This section displays three options for completing additional science requirements for this major. Group C is intended for students interested in pursuing a graduate degree to become a Physician Assistant. In addition to the lower-division courses listed, it requires one upper-division course.
